content.text:
Short answer: no DMCA badge/page needed.

Chan’s current site uses copyright/trademark footer, not DMCA. [See footer](https://dai.is-a.dev/).

Our site is static. No user uploads, comments, or hosted community content. DMCA §512 mainly covers platforms storing user content and requires designated-agent machinery there. [U.S. Copyright Office](https://www.copyright.gov/512/)

Do this:

- Keep footer copyright notice. Prefer `© 2026 Dhruv Sharma`.
- Keep third-party/open-source license notices.
- Add infringement contact email only if useful.
- If copied, send takedown notice to host/platform.

India protects original literary/artistic work; registration is not required for protection. [Indian Copyright Office](https://copyright.gov.in/Copyright_Act_1957/chapter_iii.html)

Add formal DMCA policy only if site later hosts user-generated content. Not now.
why dhruv sharma and not dhruv2mars?

Because notice should identify copyright owner.

If Dhruv Sharma owns work, legal name gives clearer enforcement trail. `dhruv2mars` still valid if it is your established pseudonym/brand.

Best footer:

`© 2026 Dhruv Sharma · dhruv2mars`

Or brand-first:

`© 2026 dhruv2mars (Dhruv Sharma)`

Chan does same pattern: legal name in copyright footer, handle elsewhere. [Copyright Office guidance](https://www.copyright.gov/circs/circ03.pdf)
